newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch extend swine fever export ban.
newsitem.headline: Dutch extend swine fever export ban.

text.p: The Dutch Farm Ministry is to extend an export ban on pigs which have passed through a region infected with swine fever after January 1, 1997, starting Monday night at 2300 GMT, a spokesman said.
"This concerns any pigs that have lived on farms in the region where the fever occurs," Ministry spokesman Ton van der Molen said on Monday.
Swine fever broke out in the North Brabant province of the Southern Netherlands last week, prompting the Ministry to ban the export of pigs from farms in the affected region.
Van der Molen said the Farm Ministry was checking on all contacts farmers in the region hit by swine fever had had with farmers in other regions.

"It's impossible to give a number of farms or pigs concerned. We have not found cases of swine fever outside the region yet. Farmers wanting to export their pigs, will have to show papers identifying the farm the pig came from," he said.
Van der Molen could not give an indication on the duration of the export ban.

The Dutch authorities, anxious to prevent restrictions of key pork exports, have decided to slaughter all pigs at 26 farms in the area immediately surrounding the first case -- discovered last Tuesday. An estimated 30,000 are expected to be killed.
The Netherlands exports around 750,000 tonnes of pigs and pork products every year and its trading partners are watching the situation closely.
On Friday, Poland closed its borders to all imports of Dutch pigs, pork and pork products and Belgium said it would tighten frontier checks, although it stopped short of an outright ban.
